sentences.text: Afrotapejara is distinguished from other tapejarids by a dorsal expansion of the front margin of the snout located a short distance from the tip.
The palate has a small boss located at the rear on the midline.
The holotype specimen FSAC-KK 5004 was found in the Kem Kem Beds and deposited in the collection of the Département de Géologie at the Faculté des Sciences Aïn Chock.
The specific name zouhri honors the Moroccan paleontologist Samir Zouhri.
CT scans revealed that a bone fragment from another taxon was used to repair damage on the upper edge of the holotype snout.
The genus Afrotapejara was established by Martill et al. in 2020 with the type species Afrotapejara zouhri and belongs to the family Tapejaridae.

Afrotapejara lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 98 to 92.5 million years ago in the Cenomanian, in what is now Africa, though other estimates suggest it lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian, between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
